seoTitle: How to Transfer Shopify Store Ownership
metaDescription: Transfer Shopify store ownership two ways: hand it to someone already on staff, or invite an outside owner straight from Settings > General without adding them first.
intro:
Selling a Shopify store, bringing on a business partner, or handing the account to whoever runs the business day-to-day all come down to one setting: store ownership. Shopify treats this as a deliberate, security-conscious action, not a simple field edit, because the store owner is the one role nobody else on the account can remove, suspend, or lock out.

Shopify actually supports this two different ways depending on whether the new owner already has a login on your store, and most guides only describe one of them. This walkthrough covers the Settings > Users route for someone already on staff, the newer Settings > General route for someone who has never touched the store before, and what has to happen on both ends before the transfer is final.

steps.heading: Open Settings in your Shopify admin
steps.body: Log into the store's admin and you land on the Home dashboard, with the sidebar showing Orders, Products, Customers, Analytics, and further down, Settings. Ownership isn't managed from any storefront-facing section — it lives under Settings, so don't go looking near Billing or Plan even though those sit close by.

image.caption: The Shopify admin Home dashboard, with the full sidebar navigation you'll use to reach Settings.

steps.heading: Open Users, and know that Shopify offers two transfer routes
steps.body:
Inside Settings, click Users to see everyone with access to the store. On a single-person store this list shows just one row: you, marked Active with a role of Store owner that can't be edited or removed the way a regular staff account can.

This Users page is where you'd transfer ownership to someone who is already a staff account on your store. It is not the only way. Shopify's own help documentation also describes a second path, under Settings > General in the "Transfer store" section, for handing the store to someone who has never had access to it at all — no staff invite required first. Pick whichever matches the new owner's situation before you continue.

image.caption: The Users screen under Settings, listing the current store owner with an Active status and a role that can't be removed like a normal staff account.

steps.heading: If they're not staff yet, add them first
steps.body:
The Users-page route only works once the new owner already exists as a user on your store. Use Add users on the Users screen to send a staff invitation to their email, and have them accept it and set up their login before you attempt the transfer.

If that extra round trip is not worth it, this is the point where the Settings > General > Transfer store option saves a step: choose "Transfer store to a new owner outside your business," confirm your identity, and enter their email directly. Shopify sends them an invitation to accept without ever making them a staff account first.

steps.heading: Open Change store ownership and enter the new owner's email
steps.body:
Using the Users-page route: once the new owner has accepted their staff invite, click Change ownership from their user page to open the Change store ownership dialog. It spells out what the role includes before you commit — the new owner can add or remove staff, change permissions, and grant access to any tool in the store, and once assigned, nobody else can remove, suspend, or delete that role. Type their email into the New store owner field carefully; it's the address the transfer confirmation goes to.

One constraint applies to either route: Shopify won't let a transfer start while the store carries an active Shopify Capital advance, Shopify Credit balance, or certain Shopify Balance obligations. Those need resolving first.

image.caption: The Change store ownership dialog, listing exactly what the new owner role includes before you enter their email address.

steps.heading: Confirm the transfer from both accounts
steps.body: After submitting the new owner's email, Shopify emails them a confirmation they have to accept from their own login before the role actually changes hands. A transfer isn't final just because you clicked the button. Check the Access page for that user, which shows the current Store owner name and email next to the Change ownership button, to confirm the swap completed instead of assuming it went through silently.

image.caption: The Access page for a user, showing the current store owner's name and email with the Change ownership button used to start a transfer.

steps.heading: Update billing and clean up access
steps.body:
Ownership moving doesn't move anything else automatically. The new owner needs to add their own payment method under Settings > Billing, and if payouts were tied to your bank account, update those details too. Business contact information — store email, phone, address — stays as it was until someone edits it in General settings.

Once the new owner's role is confirmed and billing is sorted, decide whether you still need your own staff account. If you're fully exiting, ask the new owner to remove your access once nothing is left to hand off, like unresolved orders or pending payouts.

troubleshooting.problem: Change store ownership won't let the transfer start
troubleshooting.cause: The store has an active Shopify Capital advance, an outstanding Shopify Credit balance, or a Shopify Balance obligation that Shopify requires resolved before ownership can move.
troubleshooting.fix: Pay down or resolve the balance in question, then retry the transfer.

troubleshooting.problem: The new owner says they never received anything to accept
troubleshooting.cause: Both the staff invite and the ownership confirmation are separate emails that Shopify sends outside your own admin session, and either can land in spam.
troubleshooting.fix: Have them check spam and junk folders for mail from Shopify, and resend the invite if it genuinely never arrived.

troubleshooting.problem: Your card is still being charged after the transfer completes
troubleshooting.cause: Ownership transfer moves the Store owner role only. Billing and payout details stay on the account that added them.
troubleshooting.fix: Have the new owner add their own payment method in Settings > Billing, and update payout information if it was tied to your bank account.

faq.question: Do I have to add the new owner as a staff member first?
faq.answer: Only if you use the Settings > Users route. Shopify's Settings > General > "Transfer store" option can invite someone who has never had access to the store at all, no staff invite needed.

faq.question: Can I undo a store ownership transfer?
faq.answer: Once ownership is transferred, only the new owner can grant access back to you, so confirm the recipient's email and intentions carefully before starting.

faq.question: Why isn't the ownership transfer showing up as complete?
faq.answer: Usually because the new owner hasn't accepted their staff invitation, or hasn't confirmed the ownership transfer from their own account. Both steps happen outside your admin session.

faq.question: Will billing information transfer automatically?
faq.answer: No. Billing and payout details stay tied to whoever added them, so the new owner should add their own payment method after the transfer completes.

faq.question: What stops a transfer from going through?
faq.answer: An active Shopify Capital advance, Shopify Credit balance, or certain Shopify Balance obligations block a transfer until they're resolved. Outside of that, the store owner role itself can't be removed or suspended by any other staff account.

verifiedNote: Click path and screens for the Settings > Users transfer come from a walkthrough recorded in 2025. Re-checked against Shopify's official Help Center in September 2026, which corrected two gaps this guide previously had: Shopify also offers a direct Settings > General > Transfer store path that skips adding the recipient as staff first, and a transfer is blocked while the store carries an active Shopify Capital, Shopify Credit, or certain Shopify Balance obligation.
